mcqs.question: Which of the following scenarios involves positive work done by the applied force?

options.A: A person pushes a box forward while the box moves forward.
options.B: A person pushes a wall that does not move.
options.C: A person pushes a sled backward while the sled moves forward.
options.D: A person holds a book stationary above a table.

mcqs.answer: A person pushes a box forward while the box moves forward.
mcqs.explanation: Positive work occurs when the component of the force along the displacement is in the same direction as the displacement. In option A the force and displacement are both forward, giving W = Fs cos0 = +Fs. Options B and D involve no displacement (zero work) and option C has the force opposite to the displacement (negative work).

mcqs.question: A force of 10 N acts opposite to the direction of a 5 m displacement. What is the work done by this force?
mcqs.explanation: Work is W = F s cosθ. Here θ = 180° (force opposite to displacement), so cosθ = –1. Thus W = 10 N × 5 m × (–1) = –50 J, indicating negative work. Option A ignores the sign, C would be for perpendicular or zero force, and D is numerically incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of situations both result in zero work done by the force acting?

options.A: (i) A force of 20 N acting perpendicular to a 3 m displacement; (ii) A force of 15 N acting opposite to a 4 m displacement.
options.B: (i) A force of 10 N acting on an object that does not move; (ii) A force of 5 N acting perpendicular to a 6 m displacement.
options.C: (i) A force of 8 N acting parallel to a 2 m displacement; (ii) A force of 12 N acting opposite to a 1 m displacement.
options.D: (i) A force of 0 N acting parallel to a 5 m displacement; (ii) A force of 7 N acting parallel to a 3 m displacement.

mcqs.answer: (i) A force of 10 N acting on an object that does not move; (ii) A force of 5 N acting perpendicular to a 6 m displacement.
mcqs.explanation: Work is zero when either the displacement is zero (first part of B) or the force is perpendicular to the displacement (second part of B). In A, the second situation gives negative work, not zero. In C both give non‑zero work (positive and negative). In D the first case is zero because the force magnitude is zero, but the second case gives positive work, so the pair is not both zero.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand work as a scalar quantity
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly reflects the scalar nature of work?

options.A: Work has both magnitude and direction like force.
options.B: Work can be added algebraically irrespective of direction because it is a scalar.
options.C: Work is a vector and follows vector addition rules.
options.D: Work changes sign when the coordinate system is rotated.

mcqs.answer: Work can be added algebraically irrespective of direction because it is a scalar.
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as the dot product of force and displacement, resulting in a scalar quantity. Scalars have only magnitude and can be added directly without considering direction, which is why option B is correct. Options A and C incorrectly treat work as a vector, and D is false because rotating the coordinate system does not change the scalar value of work.

mcqs.question: How is mechanical work defined for a constant force?

options.A: Product of force magnitude and displacement magnitude irrespective of direction.
options.B: Product of force magnitude, displacement magnitude, and cosine of the angle between them.

mcqs.answer: Product of force magnitude, displacement magnitude, and cosine of the angle between them.
mcqs.explanation: For a constant force, work W = F s cosθ, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement vectors. Option B states this definition precisely. Option A omits the directional factor, C describes Newton's second law, and D describes a consequence of work (the work‑energy theorem) but not the definition itself.

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: A force of 12 N acts at 60° to the direction of a 5 m displacement. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Using W = F s cosθ: W = 12 N × 5 m × cos60° = 60 N·m × 0.5 = 30 J. Option A matches this calculation. Option B would be the result if cosθ = 1, C ignores the displacement, and D would correspond to a perpendicular force (θ = 90°).

mcqs.question: Which definition best describes positive work?

options.A: Work done when the force component along displacement is in the same direction as displacement.
options.B: Work done when the force is opposite to the displacement.
options.C: Work done when the force is perpendicular to the displacement.
options.D: Work done when there is no displacement.

mcqs.answer: Work done when the force component along displacement is in the same direction as displacement.
mcqs.explanation: Positive work occurs when the component of the force along the displacement has the same direction as the displacement, giving a positive value of F s cosθ (θ < 90°). Option B describes negative work, C describes zero work, and D also leads to zero work because displacement is zero.

mcqs.question: A 20 N force acts opposite to a 3 m displacement. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work = F s cosθ. Here θ = 180°, cosθ = –1. Thus W = 20 N × 3 m × (–1) = –60 J, indicating negative work. Option B ignores the sign, C would be for zero displacement or perpendicular force, and D uses the force magnitude only without the displacement factor.
